requirements.title: A vector subscript sequence follows the values of the expression elements
requirements.source: 9.5.3.4.3 p1 sentence 1, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF157.
requirements.definition: A vector subscript designates a sequence of subscripts corresponding to the values of the elements of the vector-subscript expression. Type and rank of that expression are owned by 9.5.3.1 C929; this rule owns the value-to-sequence correspondence and preserves the expression element order, including repeated values in nondefining contexts.

pending.sequence-values-from-expression-elements: PENDING positive-control source shape: INTEGER v=[3,1] and a=[10,20,30], use a(v) in a value context. Independent oracle values [30,10]. Non-vacuous because using sorted values or triplet order produces a different list.
pending.expression-element-order-preserved: PENDING positive-control source shape: vector expression [2,4,1] and coordinate-coded literals, oracle selected values in exactly that expression order. Non-vacuous because reversing the expression changes the literal list.
pending.duplicate-values-preserved-for-value-con: PENDING positive-control source shape: vector expression [2,2,1] in a non-variable-definition value context, oracle [a2,a2,a1]. Non-vacuous because duplicate-preserving value selection differs from unique filtering; the definability restriction is separately owned by S9.5.3.4.3-004.

requirements.title: Every element of a vector-subscript expression is defined
requirements.source: 9.5.3.4.3 p1 sentence 2, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF157.
requirements.definition: Each element of the vector-subscript expression shall be defined before it contributes a subscript value. This is a definedness restriction on the expression elements, not a type/rank rule and not an invitation to read undefined storage as evidence.

pending.defined-vector-elements-control: PENDING positive-control source shape: assign every element of INTEGER v(2) before using a(v), with oracle values from distinct literals. Non-vacuous because both vector elements are consumed and changing either value changes the result.
pending.undefined-vector-element-violates-this-r: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair attributable to S9.5.3.4.3-002: declare INTEGER v(2), define only v(1), then use a(v) where type/rank and bounds would otherwise be valid if v(2)=2. Repair by assigning v(2)=2 and observe literal [a1,a2]. Do not execute or read the undefined element as an oracle.
pending.partial-definedness-runtime-condition: PENDING runtime/source plan: vector element definition depends on a branch; future oracle must prove the unassigned path by source/control-flow review or approved runtime definedness diagnostic, not by observing arbitrary selected values. Non-vacuous by paired fully assigned branch with literal oracle.

requirements.title: An array section with a vector subscript is not finalized by a nonelemental final subroutine
requirements.definition: An array section that has a vector subscript shall not be finalized by a nonelemental final subroutine. This restriction is attributable here only when the section has a vector subscript and the finalization path would use a nonelemental final subroutine; final subroutine declarations and finalization mechanics are owned by derived-type/finalization clauses.

pending.elemental-or-no-finalization-control: PENDING positive-control source shape: derived-type array with no final subroutine or only elemental finalization, vector-subscript section used in a context that would otherwise be valid. Independent oracle is a literal value from a component inquiry before finalization-sensitive scope exit. Non-vacuous because the vector section exists and has distinct selected elements.
pending.nonelemental-finalization-with-vector-se: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair attributable to S9.5.3.4.3-003: construct a type with a nonelemental final subroutine and an array section selected by a vector subscript in a finalization context. Repair only by using a triplet/nonvector section or elemental final subroutine, then observe a literal control value. Ensure declarations are otherwise valid so no 7.5 final-procedure rule is the primary violation.
pending.nonvector-section-finalization-control: PENDING positive-control contrast: same type and finalization context but section selected by triplet rather than vector subscript, with literal control oracle. Non-vacuous because the only controlled difference is vector-subscript presence.

requirements.title: A vector-subscript section with duplicate subscript values is not definable and shall not be defined or become undefined
requirements.definition: If a vector subscript has two or more elements with the same value, an array section with that vector subscript is not definable and shall not be defined or become undefined. A vector-subscript section without duplicate values is not rejected by this rule merely for appearing in a variable-definition context, although all other definability and context restrictions still apply.

pending.duplicate-vector-values-make-section-not: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair attributable to S9.5.3.4.3-004: INTEGER v=[2,2] and assignment a(v)=literal where type/rank/bounds are otherwise valid. Repair v to [2,3] and check assigned literals at a2/a3. The violation is duplicate values in a vector subscript in a definition context, not C929 or bounds.
pending.duplicate-vector-section-not-defined: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair attributable to S9.5.3.4.3-004: use a duplicate-vector section as an INTENT(OUT) or assignment target so the section would be defined. Repair to unique vector values with a literal post-assignment oracle. No other definability rule should independently reject the repaired or original source.
pending.duplicate-vector-section-not-become-unde: PENDING diagnostic-policy/source pair attributable to S9.5.3.4.3-004: use duplicate-vector section in a context that would make it become undefined, such as passing to an INTENT(OUT) dummy if otherwise permitted. Repair to unique vector values and observe a literal status set by the procedure. The negative must not rely on reading the undefined result.
pending.unique-vector-section-definition-control: PENDING positive-control source shape: INTEGER v=[3,1] with distinct values, assign a(v)=[30,10] and check a(3)==30 and a(1)==10. Non-vacuous because the section is in a variable-definition context and satisfies the no-duplicate condition.
pending.value-context-with-duplicates-control: PENDING positive-control source shape: duplicate vector [2,2,1] used only in a value context, oracle [a2,a2,a1]. Non-vacuous because duplicates are present but the section is not defined or made undefined.
